subject: Post-call: Privacy-driven deployment summary & open questions
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Privacy-driven deployment summary & open questions

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick write-up from our call so everyone has a single set of asks/assumptions — please correct if I misremember anything.

Summary of pain / drivers
- Regulatory mandate: Novamed needs full control of PHI workloads; backups must be air-gapped and retained on-prem for 7 years per audit rules.
- Network residency: Inbound inference traffic will originate from Novamed apps in the US-East VPC; model serving must not egress PHI outside your private network.
- Operational constraints: Limited ability to open outbound rules — only a handful of static IPs via outbound proxy allowed.
- Cryptography/KMS: HSM-backed key management required (FIPS 140-2/3).

High-level goals we heard
1) Proof-of-concept on-prem (non-production) within 8–12 weeks to validate latency and isolation.
2) Full production private deployment behind your perimeter for de-identified and PHI inference, with documented SLA.
3) Minimal operational burden on your infra team — Redwood to provide an ops runbook + playbooks for upgrade/fallback.

Technical constraints we captured
- No persistent outbound NAT for model runtime; egress only to our control-plane IPs (we discussed static allowlist).
- Must support air-gap for backups and the ability to physically ship encrypted backups.
- AD integration for RBAC and SSO (SAML + SCIM preferred).
- Auditing: Detailed request/response logging at token granularity retained for 90 days inside your environment; we must confirm log storage sizing.

Action items / next owners
- Novamed: send a sketch of your DMZ and preferred peering path + bandwidth baseline (Carlos) — due Tue 5/18.
- Redwood (Priyom): provide a ballpark order-of-magnitude for Private deployment (license + FY24 annual ops) and an initial SOW outline — due Wed 5/19.
- Redwood (Aditya): list of concrete firewall/IPs, ports, and TLS cipher assumptions required for the runtime to talk to the control plane (if we cannot get egress, alternate KMS/HSM UX) — due Thu 5/20.
- Both: schedule a short ops call to walk the network team through the on-prem checklist (30 minutes) — propose 5/21 or 5/24.

Attachments: redwood-onprem-checklist.xlsx (checklist), network-diagram-template.pdf (for your network sketch).

If any of the above is off, flag it; otherwise we’ll use these as the working assumptions for the POC SOW.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[hannah_schmitt@redwood.com]

From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@novamed.com>

Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novamed.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: Privacy-driven deployment summary & open questions

Thanks, Hannah — this is a helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- The air-gap requirement applies to nightly backups and the warm standby snapshot store. We still want to validate an online inference path for normalized/scrubbed PHI (non-identifiable tokens may be processed in your hosted tier only if we can guarantee no persistent storage).
- Our procurement team will also need a checklist of security evidence (SOC2, penetration test summary, any FedRAMP-equivalent artifacts if available). Procurement included here (procure@novamed.com).
- Attached is a very rough network sketch we sketched immediately after the call — please use the network-diagram-template.pdf you provided and annotate it with any required ports.

One ask from infra: can Redwood run with an outbound-proxy-only control-plane model (i.e., runtime never accepts inbound connections from Redwood, all control interactions are via outbound TLS to an allowlisted IP set)? If yes, we’ll prioritize validating that model.

Carlos
Carlos Vega
Director of Infrastructure Operations
Novamed Health Systems

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@novamed.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novamed.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 12:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Privacy-driven deployment summary & open questions

Carlos — great notes. Short answers and immediate next steps from Redwood: 

1) Outbound-proxy-only model: yes — we support a fully outbound-only control-plane tunnel mode today. That will meet your preference for no inbound connectivity to the model runtime. We’ll provide the allowlist and keep the set small (~6 IPs) and announce any changes 30 days in advance.

2) Evidence pack: we’ll assemble a compliance packet (SOC2 report, pentest summary, encryption whitepaper). I’ll push a link to a redacted compliance binder by EOD Wed 5/19.

3) Timing & ballpark: POC (on-prem, non-prod) — estimated 8–10 weeks from discovery completion; Production private deployment — 10–14 weeks depending on procurement and datacenter access windows. Ballpark commercial: one-time deployment/setup fee + annual subscription. I’ll add a conservative pricing range in the SOW draft.

4) Info we need from Novamed to finalize SOW:
   - Preferred on-prem site (address + datacenter contact)
   - Bandwidth to the control-plane endpoint and expected concurrent QPS during pilot
   - Name/contact for procurement and security (we cc’ed procurement)

Next meeting: propose Wed 5/26 10:00am ET / 07:00am PT to walk infra + security (30 min). If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments referenced: redwood-onprem-checklist.xlsx (filled-in sample will be attached in the SOW packet).

Thanks — Priyom

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@novamed.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Privacy-driven deployment summary & open questions

Hi Carlos / Marta — adding a quick technical checklist and assumptions so your infra can validate feasibility quickly. If any of these are untenable, call it out and we’ll propose alternatives.

Assumptions / runtime requirements
- Outbound-only control channel: runtime initiates TLS 1.3 outbound to allowlisted control-plane IPs (we can support mTLS).
- Ports: outbound 443 (mTLS), outbound 8443 for metrics/ops if you allow. No inbound ports required for the runtime.
- KMS/HSM: we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM, HashiCorp Vault (HSM-backed), or Thales. If you require no external KMS, we can run a local HSM appliance that we orchestrate on your subnet.
- Hardware: POC recommended profile = 2 x NVIDIA A10 / A30 (or equivalent) per host; production sizing depends on concurrency/QPS.
- Logging: request/response metadata only by default; full token-level logging must be opt-in and stored in your own S3/NFS — specify retention window.

Requests for your team
- Please confirm whether device HSM (vendor + model) is available or if Redwood should propose appliances.
- Confirm whether outbound proxy allows mTLS and SNI passthrough (we rely on SNI when cert rotation happens).
- Provide 3 representative inference requests/prompts we can use for latency profiling during the POC (can be synthetic).

If the above is good I’ll prepare a short ops playbook (10–12 pages) and a firewall matrix we can drop into your network-diagram template.

Best — Aditya
